title: Jershon and the Wilderness Report
summary: The people of Ammon were established in Jershon, where the verse also mentions an established church. Nephite armies were positioned round about Jershon and in all the borders round about Zarahemla. The verse reports that Lamanite armies had followed their brethren into the wilderness.
locations: borders round about the land of Zarahemla

explicit_facts.text: The people of Ammon were established in the land of Jershon.
The verse states "and a church also established in the land of Jershon" without identifying who established it.
Nephite armies were set round about Jershon and in all the borders round about Zarahemla.
Lamanite armies had followed their brethren into the wilderness; this is reported prior action.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A restrained establishing view may suggest the settled situation in Jershon without reenacting its establishment.
unspecified_visual_details: Terrain, distances, army sizes, clothing, equipment, and individual appearances are unspecified.
The church's physical setting is unspecified; no church building is described.

narration.text: after the people of Ammon were established in the land of Jershon, and a church also established in the land of Jershon,
behold the armies of the Lamanites had followed their brethren into the wilderness.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: No person or group is identified as establishing the church.
The Lamanite armies and their brethren belong to the reported movement, not the physically present cast.
Preserve the distinction between established conditions and previously completed movement.
prohibited_inventions: Do not reenact reported establishment or pursuit as new present-tense events.
Do not depict a simultaneous Lamanite march or confrontation.
Do not invent an actor establishing the church or assume a church building.
Do not invent commanders, dialogue, motives, or identities for their brethren.
Do not reduce Nephite positions to only the borders of Zarahemla.

title: A Tremendous Battle
summary: A tremendous battle occurred, such as had never been known among all the people in the land since Lehi left Jerusalem. Tens of thousands of Lamanites were slain and scattered abroad.

explicit_facts.text: There was a tremendous battle, such as had never been known among all the people in the land from the time Lehi left Jerusalem.
Tens of thousands of Lamanites were slain and scattered abroad.

unspecified_visual_details: The battle's precise location, participants beyond the Lamanites, weapons, tactics, and individual appearances are unspecified.
A nonrepresentational background for the narrated report is a presentation choice, not a source fact.

narration.text: And thus there was a tremendous battle; yea, even such an one as never had been known among all the people in the land from the time Lehi left Jerusalem; yea, and tens of thousands of the Lamanites were slain and scattered abroad.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Present this verse as a narrated report, not an enacted battle.
Lehi's departure from Jerusalem supplies a historical comparison, not a simultaneous event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent opposing combatants or specify who fought whom.
Do not stage combat, fleeing, or an aftermath tableau from this summarized report.
Do not depict Lehi or Jerusalem as present in the battle.
Do not invent dialogue, individual fighters, motives, or tactics.
Do not depict wounds, blood, gore, or severed body parts.

title: The People of Nephi Return
summary: There was a tremendous slaughter among the people of Nephi. The Lamanites were driven and scattered, and the people of Nephi returned to their land.

explicit_facts.text: There was a tremendous slaughter among the people of Nephi.
The Lamanites were driven and scattered.
The people of Nephi returned to their land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lamanites dispersing and the people of Nephi returning can be shown as distinct movements.
unspecified_visual_details: The terrain, route, and appearance of their land are not specified.

narration.text: the people of Nephi returned again to their land.

prohibited_inventions: Do not add named commanders, dialogue, or graphic injury.

title: Mourning Across the Land
summary: Great mourning and lamentation were heard throughout the land among the people of Nephi. Widows, fathers, daughters, and brothers mourned kindred who had been slain.
characters: People of Nephi mourning their kindred
locations: The land of the people of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: Great mourning and lamentation were heard throughout the land among the people of Nephi.
Widows mourned husbands, fathers mourned sons, daughters mourned brothers, and brothers mourned fathers.
The people mourned kindred who had been slain.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mourners may be shown expressing grief.
unspecified_visual_details: The mourners’ appearances, number, clothing, and exact surroundings are not specified.

narration.text: the cry of mourning was heard among all of them,

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earlier deaths as occurring in this scene.
Do not invent names, individual histories, or spoken words for the mourners.

title: A Day of Solemnity
summary: A sorrowful day was a time of solemnity, much fasting, and prayer.

explicit_facts.text: It was a sorrowful day and a time of solemnity.
It was a time of much fasting and prayer.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Unspecified people may be shown praying quietly.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, the people involved, and the form of their prayers.

narration.text: And now surely this was a sorrowful day; yea, a time of solemnity, and a time of much fasting and prayer.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent spoken prayers, a particular worship ceremony, or the identities of the people involved.

title: The Fifteenth Year Ends
summary: The fifteenth year of the reign of the judges over the Nephites ended.

explicit_facts.text: The fifteenth year of the reign of the judges over the Nephites ended.

unspecified_visual_details: Any visual marker or object used to signify the passing of the year.

narration.text: And thus endeth the fifteenth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a chronological summary, not a narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a judge, ceremony, or scene of a calendar being marked.

title: Account of Ammon and His Brethren
summary: The account recalls Ammon and his brethren's journeyings, sufferings, sorrows, afflictions, joy, and the reception and safety of the brethren in Jershon; it closes with a blessing.

explicit_facts.text: The account concerns Ammon and his brethren's journeyings in Nephi, their sufferings, sorrows, afflictions, joy, and the brethren's reception and safety in Jershon.
The narrator offers a blessing for their souls from the Lord, the Redeemer of all men.

unspecified_visual_details: Any visual depiction of the summarized journey, the brethren, or the blessing.

narration.text: And now may the Lord, the Redeemer of all men, bless their souls forever.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse summarizes prior events rather than narrating them as a present scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Ammon or his brethren in a new event or depict the Lord appearing; no appearance is described.

title: Wars and Contentions Recalled
summary: The account concerns wars and contentions among the Nephites and wars between the Nephites and the Lamanites. The fifteenth year of the reign of the judges ended.

explicit_facts.text: The account concerns wars and contentions among the Nephites and wars between the Nephites and the Lamanites.
The fifteenth year of the reign of the judges ended.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of any people or places associated with the account is unspecified.

narration.text: And this is the account of the wars and contentions among the Nephites, and also the wars between the Nephites and the Lamanites;
and the fifteenth year of the reign of the judges is ended

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This verse summarizes wars; it does not narrate a newly occurring battle.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific battle or invent participants, places, or dialogue.

title: Retrospective Account of Loss
summary: The span from the first year to the fifteenth brought about the destruction of many thousands of lives and awful bloodshed. Many thousands of bodies lay in the earth, while many thousands moldered in heaps upon it. Many thousands mourned lost kindred, fearing, according to the promises of the Lord, that they were consigned to endless wo.

explicit_facts.text: The span from the first year to the fifteenth brought about the destruction of many thousands of lives and awful bloodshed.
The bodies of many thousands are laid low in the earth, while those of many thousands are moldering in heaps upon the earth.
Many thousands mourn the loss of their kindred because they have reason to fear, according to the promises of the Lord, that they are consigned to endless wo.

unspecified_visual_details: No single location, gathering of mourners, or discrete moment is established.
The appearances and identities of the mourners and dead are unspecified.

narration.text: And from the first year to the fifteenth has brought to pass the destruction of many thousand lives; yea, it has brought to pass an awful scene of bloodshed.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Present this as a retrospective textual account, not a newly enacted event or continuation of an earlier scene.
The reference to endless wo reports the mourners' fear; it does not establish a visible supernatural event or confirm the fate of particular people.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage a present-tense gathering of mourners, battle, burial, or battlefield aftermath.
Do not compress losses across separate times into one depicted event.
Do not invent names, affiliations, relationships, locations, or dialogue.
Do not depict blood, wounds, gore, or severed body parts.
Do not visibly depict endless wo or invent an appearance of the Lord.

title: Mourning and Hope
summary: The report describes many thousands mourning the loss of their kindred while rejoicing in hope, and reports their knowledge, according to the promises of the Lord, concerning the departed’s never-ending happiness.

explicit_facts.text: Many thousands of others mourn the loss of their kindred.
They also rejoice and exult in hope.
The report states that they know, according to the promises of the Lord, that their departed kindred are raised to dwell at the right hand of God in never-ending happiness.

unspecified_visual_details: No setting, physical appearances, clothing, gestures, or facial expressions are specified.

narration.text: While many thousands of others truly mourn for the loss of their kindred, yet they rejoice and exult in the hope, and even know, according to the promises of the Lord, that they are raised to dwell at the right hand of God, in a state of never-ending happiness.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a continuing report, not a newly staged present-time gathering.
The verse reports hope and knowledge according to the Lord’s promises; it does not narrate a visible raising or divine appearance.
The mourners and departed kindred are mentioned in narration, not established as physically present scene participants.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the reported mourners as a present-time crowd or invent their expressions or actions.
Do not depict God, heaven, a raising, or the departed dwelling at God’s right hand.
Do not invent identities, relationships beyond kindred, dialogue, locations, or a shared moment for the reported losses.

title: The Inequality of Man
summary: The narrator reflects on the great inequality of man because of sin, transgression, and the power of the devil.

explicit_facts.text: The verse attributes the great inequality of man to sin and transgression, and to the power of the devil through cunning plans devised to ensnare people's hearts.

unspecified_visual_details: Any visual design used to accompany this teaching.

narration.text: And thus we see how great the inequality of man is because of sin and transgression, and the power of the devil, which comes by the cunning plans which he hath devised to ensnare the hearts of men.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This verse states a teaching rather than narrating a visible event. Ensnaring hearts is figurative language.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the devil, literal snares, or a supernatural event as visibly occurring.

title: Sorrow and Rejoicing
summary: The verse calls for diligence in the Lord's vineyards and identifies death and destruction as reasons for sorrow and the light of Christ unto life as a reason for joy.

explicit_facts.text: The verse calls for men to labor diligently in the vineyards of the Lord.
It identifies death and destruction among men as reasons for sorrow, and the light of Christ unto life as a reason for joy.

unspecified_visual_details: No physical setting or visible action is specified.

narration.text: And thus we see the great call of diligence of men to labor in the vineyards of the Lord; and thus we see the great reason of sorrow, and also of rejoicing—sorrow because of death and destruction among men, and joy because of the light of Christ unto life.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The vineyard and light language is teaching, not a narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not create a literal vineyard scene or depict Christ appearing.
